answer:
Pick **the dental lead-generation and appointment-setting service**, starting with follow-up on existing patient inquiries. It uses your experience, requires little capital, and offers the clearest path to recurring revenue within 20 hours a week.

The store would tie up over half your savings before proving demand. The vending route would consume most of your savings for claimed income far below your target, with servicing time and earnings still unverified.

**Days 1–30:** Keep your job and protect at least $10,000 of savings. Cap initial spending at $1,000. Check employment restrictions; avoid your employer’s patient information, equipment, time, and confidential materials. Interview 15 independent dental-office owners or managers about missed inquiries, follow-up, and appointment attendance. Offer evening/weekend follow-up only where those hours meet an actual need. Before handling patient data, establish appropriate privacy agreements and secure systems.

**Days 31–60:** Sell two paid, narrowly scoped pilots, perhaps $500–$750 per office for one month. Use offices’ existing, appropriately consented inquiries before buying advertising. Agree on baseline results and track contact rates, booked appointments, attended appointments, and your delivery hours. Keep advertising costs separate and client-funded.

**Days 61–90:** Convert successful pilots into recurring contracts, testing $1,000–$1,500 monthly pricing against measurable value. Document delivery and seek referrals. Continue only if clients renew and servicing leaves time for sales within your weekly limit; otherwise revise the offer before spending more.

Your target is **$3,400 after business expenses and taxes**, plus replacement benefits—not $3,400 revenue. Salary replacement within 18 months is ambitious. Leave employment only after six consecutive months meeting that target and building six months of personal expenses in reserve.
